=== DOCS-TRUTH ANCHORS (re-verified at trino.io/docs/467, no edits required) ===

• element_at-on-MAP (docs-truth): On `MAP(K, V)`, `element_at(map_col, key)` returns the VALUE type `V` — a SCALAR (varchar/bigint/double/etc.), NOT a collection. Returns NULL when the key is absent (no error, no exception). Verbatim from trino.io/docs/current/functions/map.html: `element_at(map(K, V), key) -> V`. Distinct from `[]` subscript which raises on missing key — `element_at` is the safe NULL-returning lookup. Resource landing: r09:554-616 (LEADING CANONICAL) + r09:578-599 (TYPE-LEVEL pin) + r09:672-683 (COALESCE-with-default idiom). For HOFs over MAP entries (filter / transform values / transform keys / inspect keys / inspect values) use `map_filter` / `transform_values` / `transform_keys` / `map_keys` / `map_values` — all documented at trino.io/docs/current/functions/map.html, all findable at r09:687-714. transform_values is the RIGHT pick when you want to REWRITE the values of a MAP in place (e.g. multiply every numeric value, lowercase every string value) — it keeps the MAP shape and only changes values, no UNNEST needed.

• day_of_week-no-dayname (docs-truth): Trino 467 has `day_of_week(ts) -> bigint` returning ISO `1=Monday..7=Sunday`. Verbatim from trino.io/docs/current/functions/datetime.html: "`day_of_week(x)` -> bigint — Returns the ISO day of the week from `x`. The value ranges from 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday)." Trino has NO `dayname()` function — confirmed via `grep -rn dayname resources/` returning empty (no false claim in any resource file). To produce the WEEKDAY NAME, either (a) `CASE day_of_week(d) WHEN 1 THEN 'Monday' WHEN 2 THEN 'Tuesday' ... WHEN 7 THEN 'Sunday' END` — explicit and self-documenting, OR (b) `format_datetime(CAST(d AS timestamp), 'EEEE')` — Joda full-day-name pattern. Both valid Trino 467; the CASE form is preferred when the column is already a DATE (no CAST needed) and you want literal control over the name (e.g. abbreviation). r07:1347 + r27:692 ISO 1-7 pin is the docs-truth anchor — synthesizable assembly is junior-engineer-tractable from the existing pins; held as WATCH-ITEM per directive.

• FILTER-on-aggregates (docs-truth): The `FILTER (WHERE <cond>)` clause is supported on EVERY Trino aggregate function — count, sum, avg, min, max, count_if, array_agg, listagg, approx_percentile, etc. Verbatim from trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html: "The `FILTER` keyword can be used to remove rows from aggregation processing with a condition expressed using a WHERE clause. This is evaluated for each row before it is used in the aggregation and is supported for all aggregate functions." Two key semantics: (1) it filters rows WITHIN the aggregate — not the rows that reach GROUP BY — so every group still appears with `0` (or NULL for non-count aggregates) when no rows match; (2) it CAN combine with DISTINCT inside the aggregate (e.g. `COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FILTER (WHERE event_name='login')`). Resource landing: r23:2057-2122 (§11 LEADING CO-CANONICAL — duplicate-subquery-collapse / conditional aggregation, iter PIN) + r23:732-770 (§3.1E count_if family with FILTER as ANSI equivalent) + r07:1862-1928 (period-total YoY single-pass conditional-aggregation pin, iter640). The right form for "total quantity sold per product across only COMPLETED orders" is `SUM(quantity) FILTER (WHERE status='completed') GROUP BY product` — single-pass, zero-group-safe (products with no completed orders emit 0 in count contexts or NULL in sum contexts, vs. WHERE which drops them entirely).
